lawyer:
Sarforaj Meah with Azahar Ullah Bhuiyan, Advocates — For the Petitioner. 
Fauzia Karim with Rebaka Sultana, Advocates —For the Opposite Party.
parties:
Golam Mowla ------ Petitioner
vs
Abdul Hashem ------ Opposite Party.
full_judgment:
The Rule has been issued at the instant of the heirs of Golam Mowla defendant of the suit on the following terms:

"Let the records be called for and a Rule be issued calling upon the opposite party No. 1 to show cause as to why the judgment and decree dated 20-11-2002 passed by the Additional District Judge, 1st Court, Noakhali in Title Appeal No. 157 of 1986 allowing the appeal and reversing the judgment and decree dated 31-5-1986 passed by the Assistant Judge, Upazila Circuit Court, Sadar, Noakhali in the Title Suit No. 230 of 1982 dismissing the suit should not be set aside or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper."

2. The plaint case, in short, is that the plaintiff instituted the Title Suit No. 230 of 1982 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Sadar Noakhali impleading the predecessor of the defendant petitioner and 3 others as proforma defendants for declaration of title of the suit schedule land of the plaint stating, inter alia, that the suit land originally belonged to Asshiny Kumar Chohoborti and Mohesh Chandra Chokroborti having 8 annas share each, Mohesh died leaving his only son Sheetal Chandra Chokroborti, Sheetal died leaving his only son Bushan Chandra Chokroborti as his heir. Bushan Chandra Chokroborti while owing and possessing of the suit land sold his share to plaintiff by registered deed dated 17-11-1972 and since purchase the plaintiff has been possessing the suit land. The plaintiff went to the Revenue Circle Office for mutating his name and came to know that defendant No. 1 mutated his name of the suit land by mutation in Miscellaneous case No. 540 and 537/72-73. The plaintiff also learned that one Devendra Kumar Chokroborti by kabala dated 18-1-1971 had sold the self same land in respect of schedule land to defendant No. 1 but Devendra Kumar Chokroborti had no title and possession in the suit land. During the period of MAR survey Devendra Kumar Chokroborti was a Peon of the local Tahshil Office and he must have included his name falsely in the MRR Khatian and such MRR khatian has created cloud in the title and possession of the plaintiff over suit land. Having learned about the wrong MRR Khatian on 2-3-1981 the plaintiff preferred appeal in the Court of additional Deputy Commissioner, Revenue but the defendant No. 1 fraudulently concealed the said appeal and thus, the plaintiff was constrained to file the suit.

3. The defendant No. 1 contested the suit by filing written statement denying the material allegations made in the plaint and stated, inter alia, that the plaintiff created the deed dated 17-11-1972 by showing false personation. Mohesh Chandra Chokroborti had no son namely Sheetal Chandra Chokroborti and Sheetal Chandra had no son namely Bushan Chandra and those alleged persons had no title and possession of the suit land but Mohesh had died issueless and as a result his brother Asshini inherited his share. Asshini died leaving his only son Devendra Kumar Chokroborti who became owner in possession of the suit land. Accordingly, MRR Khatian was finally prepared and published in the name of Devendra Kumar Chokroborti and Devendra while on owning and possessing the suit land by paying rent and taxes sold the suit land by registered kabala dated 18-1-1971 along with other lands to the defendant No. 1 and handed over possession and since purchase the defendant No. 1 has been owning and possessing the suit land by mutating his name, paying all rent and Taxes of the government and prayed for dismissal of the suit.

4. The Assistant Judge, Sadar Noakhali heard the suit. Plaintiff examined 5 witnesses and the defendant examined 4 witnesses to prove their respective case and also marked the exhibits and ultimately dismissed the suit by his judgment and decree dated 31-5-1986 and 7-6-1986 respectively.

5. The plaintiff having been aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment and decree of the trial Court had preferred title Appeal No. 157 of 1986 in the Court of District Judge, Noakhali and eventually the appeal was heard by Additional District Judge, 1st Court, Noakhali who allowed the appeal by his judgment dated 20-11-2002 and the decree signed on 26-11-2002.

6. The above petitioner being the heir of the defendant Golam Mowla having been aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment and decree passed by the Additional District Judge, has preferred this revisional application before this Court and having heard the learned Advocate for the petitioner this Court issued the Rule as aforesaid.

7. Mr Sarforaj Meah, Advocate along with Mr Md Azahar Ullah Bhuiyan, Advocate and Mr Lokman Hossain, Advocate appearing on behalf of the defendant petitioner, has taken me through the judgments of both the Courts, plaint, written statement and the evidence of the parties and submitted that the judgment of the Appellate Court is not a proper judgment al reversal as the Appellate Court has not reversed the findings of the trial Court arrived at on proper consideration of the materials on record. The learned Advocate at the very outset submitted that the Exhibit 2 is a void document and also drawn my attention to the findings of the trial Court:

“প্রদর্শনী ২ সম্পর্কে প্রতিদন্ধী বিবাদী পক্ষ আরেকটি যে অতি গুরুত্ব পূর্ণ আপত্তি আনিয়াছেন তাহা হইতেছে এই যে, উক্ত প্রদর্শনী ২ এর ১ নং তপশীলে বর্ণিত সম্পত্তিতে উক্ত প্রদর্শনী-২ এর দাতার কোন প্রকার স্বত্ব দখল ছিল না। শুধু মাত্র বেগমগঞ্জ রেজিস্ট্রি অফিসে রেজিস্ট্রি করার খাতিরে উক্ত ১ নং তপশীলের সম্পত্তি ভূয়া ভাবে অন্তর্ভুক্ত করা হইয়াছে। এই ব্যাপারে বিবাদী পক্ষ গুরুতর আপত্তি উথাপন করিয়াছেন। এবং এই প্রসঙ্গে ১৫২নং মহেশ পুর মৌজার ৬০ নং খতিয়ান প্রদর্শনী খ(২) দাখিল করিয়াছেন। যাহা পযালোচনা করিলে স্বীকৃতি মতেই দেখা যায় যে, উক্ত ৬০ নং খতিয়ান জনৈক নিমচান রাজের নামে রেকর্ড হইয়াছে।

বাদী তাহার প্রদর্শনী ২ এর উল্লেখ করে বলিতে চান যে, উক্ত নিমচান হইতে বাসা প্রদর্শনী ২ এর ১ নং তপশীলে সম্পত্তিতে খরিদ সূত্রে মালিক। কিন্তু এই ব্যাপারে বাদী কোন প্রকার কাগজ পত্র দাখিল করেন নাই কিংবা করিতে পারেন নাই। অথচ তাহা প্রমাণের ভার সমস্তই বাদীর উপরে পড়ে। কারণ প্রতিদ্বন্দ্বি বিবাদী ৬০ নং খতিয়ান প্রদর্শনী খ(২) দাখিল করিয়া দাবী করিতেছেন যে, বাদীর দাতা ভূষণ চক্রবর্তী নালিশ প্রদর্শনী ২ এর ১ নং তপশীলের সম্পত্তিতে কোন ভাবেই মালিক নহে। অথচ বাদী বলিতেছেন যে ভূষণ চন্দ্র খরিদ সূত্রে মালিক ছিল। সুতরাং বাদী যদি ভূষণ মালিক ছিল বলে প্রমাণ দিতে পারেন তবে স্বাভাবিক ভাবেই বিবাদীর কথা গৃহীত হইবে। এবং আলোচ্য ক্ষেত্রেও তাহাই হইয়াছে। এইরুপ সম্পত্তি তাহার বিক্রি করার কোন অধিকার নাই। এবং অনাধিকার ভ��বে দাতার সম্পত্তি ভিন্ন অন্য সম্পত্তি অন্তর্ভুক্ত করে প্রদর্শনী ২ রেজিস্ট্রি করার কারণে প্রদর্শনী ২ এর কোন আইনগত মূল্য বলিয়া আমি মনে করি না।”

and also drawn my attention to the findings of the Appellate Court and pointed out that the Appellate Court has not reversed this specific findings of the trial Court which is the main crux of the case and, thereby has committed error of law which is an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. The learned Advocate then drew my attention to the schedule of the plaint and also evidence of the PW 1 and submitted that the plaintiff cunningly has not brought the land of Mouja Moheshpur PS Begumgonj area being 0.5 decimals in the schedule of the plaint and also made no statement in the plaint as well as in the deposition of the PW 1 as the plaintiff had shown fictitious land for the purpose of the registration of the deed only in violation of the provision of section 28 of the Registration Act 1908 and further submitted that the deed being void the plaintiff is not entitled to any relief. He then refers to a decision in the case of Ranju Roy vs Jibesh Ranjan Roy reported in 14 MLR (AD) 18. Their Lordships held in paragraph 6, the relevant passage from the aforesaid paragraph is quoted below:

"Moreover the plaintiff, who examined him as PW 1 in his cross-examination admitted that he started to reside in the suit homestead as a licensee under Manindra; further the plaintiff had set up his claim of possession firstly as a licensee under Manindra and thereafter on the strength of the kabala deed dated 23-6-1985 executed by Arun Chandra Shil in his favour, the subsequent claim of the plaintiff on the basis of Kabala dated 23-6-1986 has no basis at all because admittedly the suit land is situated within the territorial jurisdiction of Derai Sub-registry Office but the plaintiff's kabala dated 23-6-86 allegedly executed by Arun Chandra Shil was registered at the Sunamganj Sub-Registry Office including fictitious land only to attract the jurisdiction of Sunamganj Sub-Registry Office and further, the plaintiff had failed to produce any document at the trial to show that the land included in the kabala belonged to Arun Chandra Shil nor any evidence is available on record to show that the said land belonged to Arun Chandra Shil in view of the above the kabala dated 23-6-85, if any, being registered offending the provision of section 28 of the Registration Act is nothing but a void deed."

8. To support his contention another decision in the case of Anwar Hossain vs Abdul Hossain Mollah reported in 44 DLR 79 paragraph 15 which runs thus:

"The learned Advocate also urged that fraud was practiced on the Registration Act, inasmuch as the land conveyed as per Exhibit A lies within the territorial jurisdiction of Pangsha Sub-Registry Office, but two decimals of land lying within the jurisdiction of Baliakandi Sub-Registry Office was included in the sale deed to invoke the jurisdiction of Baliakandi Sub-Registry Office and thus a fraud was practised under Registration Act. Section 28 of Registration Act speaks that document which affects immovable property shall be presented for registration in the office of sub-registrar within whose sub-district the whole or some portion of the property to which such documents relate is situated. In the instant case it has already been mentioned above that two decimals of land whose ownership having not been disclosed has been included in the impugned sale deed Exhibit A to attract the jurisdiction of Baliakandi Sub-registry Office. It is settled law that where no part of property to which document relates is situated within the jurisdiction of Sub-registrar, the Sub-registrar has no jurisdiction to register the document and registration if executed will be fraud. The defect of jurisdiction is not a mere procedure and it is not cured by section 87. The learned 1st Appellate Court made an attempt to defend this action on the ground that plaintiffs being a party to the deed were debarred from challenging it, but the learned 1st Appellate Court committed gross error interpreting the facts in this regard. Plaintiff-appellants are not party to the deed Exhibit A and, as such, are entitled to call in question the legality of registration of the sale deed Exhibit A. The 1st Appellate Court wrongly held the plaintiffs-appellants robe the party to the deed Exhibit A."

9. The learned Advocate has also placed the findings of the trial Court that the trial Court specifically held that the suit is barred by limitation and also has drawn my attention to the suggestion given by the plaintiffs during cross examination of the DW 1 inasmuch as :

“১৯৭৩ সনে বাদীর সঙ্গে নালিশী সম্পত্তি নিয়ে কোন সংগষ হওয়া বা তাহা মৌঃ হাবিবুর রহমান এর মোট ১ মাসের শালিশ মান্য করায় উক্তিমাত্র নহে। (with objection) ১৯৭৪ ইং সনে এসডিও আদালতে ৭৪৯ নং পি, মকদ্দমা আমি দায়ের করি নাই (with objection)”

but plaintiffs stated the date of knowledge in the plaint as on 2-3-1981 which is false and the trial Court upon consideration of the materials on record correctly held that the suit is barred by limitation but the Appellate Court has not reversed this specific findings of trial Court and thereby, committed fundamental error of law occasioning failure of justice.

10. The learned Advocate for the petitioner has submitted further that PW 2, a scribe of the deed in his evidence stated that on the date of registration of the deed the Sub-registrar Sadar, Noakhali was absent and Sub-registrar Begumgonj had authority to admit the registration of the deed but no paper has been produced before the Court to prove such contention. It is true the plaintiff has not exhibited any paper before the Court to prove his such contention.

11. Ms Rebeka Sultana along with Ms. Farzia Karim the learned Advocates, appearing on behalf of the plaintiff-opposite party, has candidly supported the judgment of the Appellate Court and submitted that the Appellate Court having regard to the provisions of Order XII rule 31 has dearly reversed the finding of the trial Court and accordingly, recorded findings and having been satisfied upon discussion of the materials on record has decreed the suit in all counts and thereby, the appellate Court committed no error of law which calls for no interference by this Court and that the judgment of the Appellate Court is a proper judgment of reversal.

12. When this Court, has drawn the attention of the learned Advocate for the opposite party as to the non inclusion of the land of Begumgonj PS in the schedule of the plaint, She finds difficult to give reply as to non inclusion of land of the Begumgonj in the schedule of the plaint as well as prayer to that effect.

13. I have perused the judgment of the trial Court and found that the trial Court has adverted to the materials, inasmuch as the plaint, written statement and also the evidence and the exhibits and came to the findings that the suit is not maintainable as the plaintiff instituted the suit in 1982 having knowledge on 2-3-1981 though the land allegedly purchased on 17-11-1972 and the trial Court also came to the findings that the plaintiff for the purpose of registration of the land have shown land of Begumgonj PS showing fictitious land in violation of the provision of section 28 of the Registration Act and thus dismissed the suit.

<u>14. The appellate Court recorded findings that the Exhibit 2 kabala deed dated 17-11-1972 is a genuine deed and the land was purchased from the heirs of Mohendra and registered the deed having observed the formalities. The Appellate Court also believed the date of cause of action discarding the findings of the trial Court. On further scrutiny of the judgment of the Appellate Court, it appears that the Appellate Court has not reversed the findings of the trial Court regarding the registration of the deed at Begumgonj Sub-registrar office (Exhibit 2) a different place showing some fictitious land belonged to one Nim Chand Raj a different person.</u>

<u>15. I have also found that the plaintiff has not made any pleadings/statements and prayer regarding the land situated at Begumgonj and also led no evidence in respect of the said land and the same has not been also brought in the schedule of the plaint. On perusal of the cross examination of the DW 1 as quoted above, it appears that the plaintiff gave suggestion about certain litigation of 1973-74 which clearly indicated that the plaintiff had knowledge about the MRR Khatian appearing in the name of the defendant in 1973-74 but the suit admittedly instituted in 1982 showing knowledge on 2-3-1981 and the evidence and suggestion has clearly indicated that the suit was instituted after about 9 years and thereby, the suit is barred by limitation. Admittedly, the property of schedule 2 and 3 of Exhibit 2 is situated under Noakhali Sadar Sub-registry office and in both the schedules the area is 0.70 decimals. The land shown in schedule 1 of the aforesaid Exhibit 2 is situated at Begumgonj and the sub-registry office is also at Begumgonj. On the scrutiny of the Exhibit 'Kha' (2) it appears that the land belonged to one Nim chand Raj but not to Sree Bushan Chandra Chokroborti and from the evidence it can clearly be inferred that the land shown in the Begumgonj PS is a fictitious land which the plaintiff has included in the schedule of Exhibit 2 kabala deed to get the deed registered in the Begumgonj sub-registry office, which apparently does not belong to Sr. Bushan Chandra Chokroborti. The plaintiff has failed to produce any document of Begumgonj that the land shown in the Exhibit 2 belonged to Sree Bushey Chandra Chokroborti nor any evidence is brought on record to show that the said land belonged to Bushan Chandra Chokroborti.</u>

<u>16. In view of the above, the kabala dated 17-11-1972 having been registered in violation of section 28 of the Registration Act is nothing but a void deed, rather fraud was practiced under the Registration Act and as a result, the plaintiff is not entitled to the decree. I have also perused the decisions cited above and I am of the view that the submissions made by the teamed Advocate of the defendant-petitioner find support in the aforesaid decisions and also I am of the view that the submissions of the teamed Advocate have sufficient substance that the Appellate Court failed to reverse the findings of the trial Court on material points as to maintainability of the suit and also as to status of the Exhibit 2 the kabala dated 17-11-1972 and, as such, it reveals that the judgment of the Appellate Court is not a proper judgment of reversal as the Appellate Court has failed to reverse the specific findings of the trial Court passed on proper appreciation of the materials on record.</u>

17. In the premises aforesaid, I find merit in the Rule.

18. In the result, the Rule is made absolute without any order as to costs. The impugned judgment and decree of the Appellate Court passed in Title Appeal No. 157 of 1986 are set aside and the judgment and decree of trial Court are restored and thereby, the suit is dismissed.

Send down the lower Courts records immediately.

End.
